title: Reason Code 36: the account is locked out
plain_english: The account exceeded the domain's failed-logon threshold and is locked. With Wi-Fi this is very often self-inflicted: a phone or laptop with an old saved password retries every few seconds, locks the account, and keeps it locked. Unlocking without finding that device only buys a few minutes.

any: exceeded the maximum allowed number of failed attempts

causes.cause: A device with a stale saved Wi-Fi or VPN password is retrying in a loop.
causes.next_check: Filter the 6273 events for this account and read the Calling Station Identifier values: the MAC that appears every few seconds is the culprit; forget the network on that device.

causes.cause: A genuine lockout after real failed attempts.
causes.next_check: Unlock in Active Directory Users and Computers (Account tab), then confirm the source with event 4740 on the PDC emulator, which names the caller computer.

causes.cause: The lockout threshold is too low for 802.1X retry behaviour, where one wrong password produces several failures per minute.
causes.next_check: Review Account Lockout Policy (threshold and observation window) with the retry rate of your supplicants in mind.
